pov1.prompt: A man's own view from the driving seat of a closed 1931 sedan, his eyes level with the top of the steering wheel, travelling down an empty straight country road at night. Along the bottom of the picture are a large thin black steering wheel and his two hands resting on its rim at ten and two, relaxed, in oxblood leather gloves, a narrow strip of mustard check cuff showing at each wrist. Behind the wheel a flat painted steel dash, the dull green of old enamel, holds two round cream-faced gauges marked only with ticks. Above it, a tall upright windscreen divided by a slim metal frame, with a dark cloth roof lining across the top of the picture and thick dark pillars at both sides. Through the glass, a long bottle-green bonnet with a centre hinge and a small upright radiator cap, and past it the domed tops of two separate mudguards with a round lamp standing on each. The headlamps throw a weak yellow pool down thirty yards of pale dry macadam, which fades to black beyond. A row of bare wooden telegraph poles runs along one verge. Far down the road, one small building stands on the verge, its wall painted crimson, lit by a single bare bulb over a shut door. Above a black line of low hills, the last of the dusk is a band of deep indigo with some stars. The road is otherwise empty and nothing is in the air. Dye-rich colour, soft grain, honest darkness in the cabin with only a little of the headlamp glow on the gloves.
pov1.why: With one straight road, one lit building and nothing loose in frame, the only thing the clip has to do is drive forward, which removes every object that morphed last time.

pov3.prompt: A driver's view from behind the wheel of a 1932 open tourer rolling at steady speed along a dockside street at dusk, heading straight for the mouth of a brick road tunnel. At the bottom of the picture, a slim black steering wheel with one hand at the top of its rim in an oxblood leather glove, and the other glove resting on the round black knob of a long floor gear lever, a line of mustard check cuff at each wrist. A folding upright windscreen in a plain nickel frame stands square to the road, and beyond it a long mustard-yellow bonnet with side louvres runs out to two round lamps standing on separate black mudguards. The road is dry granite setts with a pair of tram rails running dead straight down the middle, carrying the eye to the tunnel a hundred yards off: a tall arch of soot-dark brick, its inside true black except for a line of small amber lamps curving away along the roof. One small ruby tail lamp shows far inside, the only other vehicle in the picture. On one side, a row of tall warehouses in flat painted colours, oxblood, faded teal and tobacco brown, with their big loading doors shut and one lit lamp over each door. On the other side, a low stone wall with black water beyond it and one moored barge, unlit. The sky over the warehouses is a dim plum going to rust at the horizon, and that light falls from ahead onto the bonnet and the backs of the gloves. The horizon is level. The street is empty of people. Fine grain, heavy dye colour, deep shadow under the wall.
pov3.why: The level car, straight rails and fixed tunnel keep it grounded with no jump to fake, and the black arch gives an 8-second drive a physical dark to end in for a cut.

rods1.prompt: Two stripped-down 1929 racing roadsters run side by side across a dry alkali lakebed in the last hour of sun, seen in side view from a camera at hip height on a car keeping pace thirty metres away. Both cars point to the right of the frame, parallel, on the same heading. The nearer car, in oxblood red enamel, is half a length ahead; the farther car, in mustard yellow, sits just behind it and beyond it, its whole outline clear of the red one. Each is a tall, narrow, upright machine: a square radiator shell, separate curved mudguards, a flat running board, thin wire-spoked wheels on narrow tyres pressed firmly on the ground, and a small upright windscreen. Each driver is a grown man in a brown leather cap and goggles, both hands low on a wooden wheel. Bodies are plain and unlettered. A low, even trail of pale dust stretches straight back to the left edge from each rear wheel. The sun sits behind the camera and lays long black shadows under the cars on the cracked pinkish-white ground. The mountains behind are a band of dark plum beneath a deepening blue sky, softened by a gentle horizontal blur, while the cars stay sharp and their spokes blur into grey discs. Clear lakebed fills the space ahead of the lead car. Coarse colour film grain, dense reds and yellows, edge to edge in 16:9.
rods1.why: Two cars on one parallel heading, held level by a pacing camera, can simply keep running in place while the background slides, leaving nothing to reverse, jump or collide.

rods4.prompt: A long lens looks up a wide concrete flood channel at dusk in 1931, from knee height on the dry floor, a little right of the centre line so the three road bridges step away toward the left instead of lining up. The nearest arch crosses the top of the frame, its underside almost black. Two 1930 roadsters come toward the camera along the flat floor, one behind the other, just emerging from the shadow of the middle arch and still well down the channel. The lead car is chalky turquoise, the second mustard yellow, offset a little to its left so both can be seen. They are tall, narrow and upright: square radiators, separate curved mudguards, running boards, thin spoked wheels and small upright windscreens, with two round lamps lit a dull yellow on each. All four wheels of each car sit level on the concrete. Each driver is a grown man in a leather cap, sitting straight up. A thin, still ribbon of water runs along the middle of the floor beside them, carrying one long dim bar of the sky; the concrete around it is pale, stained with rust and only damp in patches. Behind the far bridge the sky is deep plum fading to dull rose at the horizon. One iron lamp on the far bridge throws a small amber pool on the wall below it. The sloped banks are empty and already in deep blue-grey shadow. Fine colour film grain, edge to edge in 16:9.
rods4.why: Two level cars driving straight up a flat floor with one still strip of water and empty banks gives one plain event, with no wall-riding, spray or onlookers to exaggerate or morph.

safe3.prompt: Seen from the catwalk of a rooftop water tower, looking steeply down over a corroded iron rail that crosses the lower right corner close to the lens and out of focus, an inland brick district of a 1928 city an hour after sundown, with a sliver of dull violet sky along the top edge of the frame. One wide, straight avenue runs through the picture from the upper right to the lower left, paved in pale dry granite setts the colour of old bone, with a raised kerb and a strip of pavement down each side, iron lamp posts at even intervals throwing round pools of yellow light on the stone, and closed shopfronts under oxblood and bottle-green awnings along its length, so that it shows as the brightest, plainest shape in the picture and can only be a street. Three black sedans stand parked and dark against the kerb. In the middle of the avenue a single tall, upright sedan in egg-yolk yellow, small in the frame but large enough to read its boxy cabin, separate black mudguards, running boards and spoked wheels, points straight down the road toward the lower left with its two round headlamps laying short beams on the setts ahead of it. Behind it a taut chain runs back along the centre of the road to a small dark iron safe lying flat on the stone, and from the point where the iron grinds on the granite one thin bright thread of orange sparks stretches back along the same line for the length of a block, dulling to red as it cools and tinting the setts beneath it. Far up the avenue, two small white headlamps of one following car point the same way along the road. Every other part of the view is rooftop: tar and water tanks and chimney stacks, mostly dark, with a few long skylights glowing amber, one rooftop painted in faded jade, and a row of bulb signs seen from behind so they show only as scaffolding and rows of dots. The whole district is dry land, roofs and paved road from edge to edge, with no river, canal or bridge anywhere in it. A long-lens view with flattened layers of buildings, deep plum shadows, saturated film colour and a fine grain, filling the entire 16:9 frame without any margin.
safe3.why: The canal and bridge are gone and the road is now a pale, kerbed, lamp-lit street, which leaves nothing dark and wet for a car to appear to drive on, and the car, chain and spark line all sit on one straight axis so the only motion is forward.

safe1.prompt: The instant a small safe leaves a wall, seen from across a narrow back alley at night in 1928, the camera at chest height against the opposite wall with a rusted iron drainpipe cut off by the left edge of the frame. An egg-yolk yellow sedan with a tall upright body, separate black mudguards, a running board and spoked wheels stands at a hard angle on the right, its rear wheels spinning on wet-dark cobbles and throwing thick grey tyre smoke, lit deep red by its two small tail lamps. From its rear axle a heavy chain runs dead straight, rigid as a bar, across the alley and into a ragged hole in an oxblood brick wall with a flaking bottle-green painted band. The safe, a squat cast-iron box in chipped forest-green enamel with a brass dial, hangs tilted in the air a foot outside the hole with the chain wrapped around it, while bricks, mortar and pieces of green wall fall around it through a cloud of pale dust. One bare amber bulb in a tin shade above a wooden back door, high on the left, is the only other light, so the dust glows amber on one side and red on the other, and the far end of the alley drops into true black. A man leans far out of the sedan's rear window, big enough in the frame to read clearly, dark overcoat collar turned up, both leather-gloved hands gripping the door. He has twisted round so the front of his head faces the camera almost square on, turned only slightly toward the hole in the wall, and the whole front of his mask is lit by the amber bulb. His whole head is inside a hand-knitted balaclava of marine-blue wool, slightly uneven, with a ribbed neck tucked into the collar and continuous knit running unbroken across the place where eyes, nose and mouth would be. One thin ring of cream wool, chain-stitched by hand, is a wide oval that fills the whole front of his head, reaching from his brow to his chin and from cheek to cheek. Inside that ring, level with his left eye and close against the ring at the two o'clock position as we look at him, sits one small triangle of solid red felt with rounded corners, point downward, its hand-cut edge sewn down with tiny black running stitches. The middle of the ring and everything to the left of the triangle is bare blue knit. Falling bricks are slightly blurred, while the chain, safe and mask are sharp. Rich saturated colour film with visible grain and hard shadows on the brick, the picture running edge to edge across the whole 16:9 frame.
safe1.why: The scene stays word for word apart from the period wording on the car, while the head now faces the camera and the triangle is anchored to his left eye and a clock position on a much larger ring, which is where it sits on the approved jeweller's-shop mask.
